iot-core-the-message-broker.core: IoT Core is a managed MQTT (and HTTPS/WebSocket) broker for millions of devices. Each device authenticates with an X.509 certificate (mutual TLS) registered as a 'thing', is authorised by IoT policies scoped to topics, and publishes or subscribes to hierarchical topics. QoS 0/1 and persistent sessions handle unreliable networks.

first_principles.problem: A fleet of 100,000 sensors needs secure, scalable messaging over flaky cellular links.
truths: Devices are constrained and intermittently connected.

analogy.title: A post office for devices
analogy.story: Every device has its own ID card and can only post to and collect from its own mailboxes.
analogy.breaks: Post offices deliver once; MQTT QoS 1 may redeliver, so handle duplicates.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: A stolen device can only publish its own telemetry.

check.q: How do IoT devices authenticate to IoT Core?
check.a: Typically with X.509 client certificates over mutual TLS.

device-shadows-talking-to-ghosts.core: A device shadow is a JSON document in the cloud holding a device's reported state (what it says) and desired state (what apps want). Apps update desired state even while the device is offline; when it reconnects, it receives the delta, applies it and reports back. Named shadows let one device have several state documents.

first_principles.problem: A mobile app can't change a thermostat's setting because the device is temporarily offline.
truths: Apps need a consistent view of state.

analogy.title: A note left on the fridge for someone who's out
analogy.story: When they get home, they read it, do it and write back 'done'.
analogy.breaks: Notes can be ignored; shadows keep sending the delta until reported matches desired.

check.a: The differences between desired and reported state that the device should act on.

iot-greengrass-lambda-at-the-edge.core: IoT Greengrass is an edge runtime that runs components (Lambda functions, containers, ML inference, protocol adapters) on local gateways or devices, processes data locally, works offline, syncs with IoT Core when connected and is deployed and updated from the cloud. It reduces latency, bandwidth and dependence on connectivity.

first_principles.problem: Streaming raw high-frequency sensor data to the cloud is costly, and decisions need sub-second response even offline.

analogy.title: A local branch manager with authority
analogy.story: Makes day-to-day decisions on site and sends headquarters a summary each evening.
analogy.breaks: Managers improvise; components only do what was deployed to them.

example.title: Vibration anomaly detection
flow: Greengrass ML component flags anomalies locally

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: 99% less data sent; instant safety response.

check.q: Why process IoT data with Greengrass instead of in the cloud?
check.a: To reduce latency and bandwidth, and keep working when connectivity is lost.

iot-rules-engine-routing-data-to-aws-ser.core: The IoT Rules Engine evaluates SQL-like statements on MQTT messages as they arrive (SELECT temp, deviceId FROM 'fleet/+/telemetry' WHERE temp > 80) and routes matching data to actions: Lambda, DynamoDB, S3, Kinesis, Firehose, SQS, SNS, Timestream, IoT Events and more, with error actions for failed deliveries.

first_principles.problem: A Lambda subscribes to all telemetry just to filter and forward a tiny fraction.
derivation: Write **rule SQL** with topic filters and WHERE clauses.
Use **Basic Ingest** ($aws/rules/) to cut messaging cost.

analogy.title: A mail sorting machine with rules
analogy.story: Letters matching certain criteria are routed to specific bins automatically.
analogy.breaks: Sorting machines handle letters once; rules can send one message to several destinations.

steps.label: Actions
steps.detail: SNS alert + DynamoDB write; error action to S3.

code.text:
SELECT topic(2) AS deviceId, temp, timestamp() AS ts
FROM 'fleet/+/telemetry'
WHERE temp > 80

check.a: Sends messages directly to rules via $aws/rules/ topics without broker publish costs.
